outcome: Severe perineal trauma (Obstetric and Anal Sphincter Injury [OASIS], third- and fourth-degree perineal tear)
cohort: The study included 2846 women delivering in a tertiary high-risk pregnancy facility in Brazil between April 2017 and February 2019, who were mostly white (66.3%) and primiparous (52.1%).
finding: After multivariate analysis, a larger neonatal head circumference was the only independent risk factor, increasing the risk for severe perineal trauma by 86%.
mod_finding: Forceps delivery was identified as a risk factor for OASIS in univariate analysis (OR, 3.68), while selective episiotomy was not associated with OASIS.
